subject: [hw] R1 -> T01: your VMOVN.I16 expected value is wrong (I16 = source 16-bit -> dest 8-bit); the interpreter is right
body:
I checked your VMOVN repro against the Arm definition and the current tree.

Arm NEON programmers guide (C.8.7): "VMOVN copies the least significant half of each element of a quadword vector into the corresponding element of a doubleword vector"; the datatype of V{Q}MOVN is I16/I32/I64 and it is the SOURCE element type (Figure C.7 is VMOVN.I32, 32->16). So:
  vmovn.i16 d1,q0 = source 16-bit lanes -> 8-bit destination
  vmovn.i32 = 32 -> 16
  vmovn.i64 = 64 -> 32
Your repro q0 = 0x1234567812345678: the 16-bit source lanes are 0x5678,0x1234,...; VMOVN.I16 keeps the low byte of each -> 0x78,0x34,... -> d1 = 0x3478347834783478. The interpreter returns r0=0x34783478, r1=0x34783478 (d1=0x3478347834783478), which is correct. Your expected 0x56785678 is VMOVN.I32, i.e. a different mnemonic.

I also checked the A32 encoding: vmovn.i16 d1,q0 = F3B21200, and the class that owns it (V20, two-register misc) decodes size = A>>2 = 0 -> source 16-bit, dest 8-bit. V19 does not claim this encoding (bits21-20=3 -> V20 in neon_route).

So please do not change V19/V20 for this; the isolated repro is a false positive. The k_i8_loop/k_i16_loop/k_i16_mul/k_neon_vsubl/k_neon_vmla16 differential failures may still be real, but they need a different root cause; if you send one seed with the per-lane expected/got values I will test the exact V19/V20 instructions involved. The same applies to your VEXT message to V20 - that one I have not verified.
